teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: Generated documentation is public and can drift from executable behavior. Review the actual schema alongside HTTP outcomes and safe example data.

teaching_blocks.title: The rule and its boundary
teaching_blocks.content: Retrieve /openapi.json and inspect the router's paths, parameters, request schemas, response schemas and security requirements as public contract artifacts.

teaching_blocks.title: How to use the rule
teaching_blocks.content: Compare generated requiredness, types, constraints and output fields with executable input and output behavior to identify drift between documentation and the accepted or emitted contract. Compare documented success and expected-error statuses with exercised HTTP outcomes, because an additional response declaration does not prove the handler actually emits that outcome. Audit public examples and descriptions for secrets and sensitive personal data, and ensure examples validate against the model rather than publishing realistic private values. Check that public security schemes and operation requirements describe the configured bearer and established issuer contract and do not introduce an undeployed password grant.

teaching_blocks.title: Reason through an example
teaching_blocks.content: Retrieve /openapi.json and inspect paths, parameters, input/output schemas and security requirements. Compare requiredness, types, constraints and emitted fields with behavior, then compare documented success and expected-error statuses with exercised outcomes. Validate examples and remove secrets or sensitive personal data from descriptions. Check that security entries match the bearer and established issuer contract without adding an undeployed password grant.

teaching_blocks.title: Keep this distinction
teaching_blocks.content: An additional response declaration does not prove that outcome occurs. Public examples must also be safe and model-valid.

visual_anchor.purpose: Show one router's generated declarations beside model definitions, exercised HTTP outcomes and configured security metadata, with drift and sensitive public examples visibly marked.

practice_anchor.objective: Retrieve /openapi.json and audit one existing router's generated contract against its models, supplied non-authentication HTTP outcomes and established security configuration. Record drift and unsafe public examples without adding authentication or authorization tests.
practice_anchor.success: The audit covers paths, parameters, request and response schemas, requiredness, types, constraints, output fields, documented statuses, examples, descriptions and security requirements. Findings distinguish declarations from observed behavior, identify sensitive or invalid examples, and flag security declarations that differ from the deployed contract.

live_code.required_skill: Inspect generated OpenAPI with Python and compare its declarations with existing models, exercised HTTP evidence and configured security metadata.
allowed_syntax: String, numeric, boolean, list and dictionary literals
blocked_syntax: New authentication or authorization test functions
Assertions testing invalid-token rejection or permission enforcement
live_code.starter_state_intent: Provide an existing application and one router, its request and response models, synthetic public examples, previously exercised non-authentication request/response evidence, and the established bearer and issuer configuration. Include an incomplete audit script that retrieves the schema and collects findings using the router's existing names only.
live_code.observable_success: The completed script retrieves the generated schema, inspects the selected router and referenced schemas, compares declarations with supplied behavior evidence, validates synthetic examples against existing models, and records documentation findings. Security review compares declarations with supplied configuration rather than exercising authentication or authorization.
